papers.title: Evaluating Runtime Prediction and Conservative Walltime Policies in HPC Systems
authors: Hector Romero Ugalde, Youssef Faqir-Rhazoui, Marlon Funk, Jesus Gorro\~nogoitia Cruz
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.27755v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient use of large-scale supercomputing systems depends on accurate runtime estimation and walltime selection. To avoid premature termination, users often overestimate walltime, leading to poor resource utilization and reduced scheduling efficiency. This paper presents a predictor-agnostic framework for safe walltime recommendation in production HPC environments. Rather than proposing a new runtime prediction model, the primary contribution is the SAFE decision layer, which converts predicted runtimes into conservative bounded walltime recommendations suitable for deployment. papers.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.24865v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade, the model built for rumour and adoption spread on social networks, now embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and space are one coupled system, and this feedback, not any tuning, makes the coordination self-limiting. papers.title: Budgeted Admission from Timestamped Capacity Records in Shared Clusters
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.28392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A cluster admission gate can receive a capacity record that no longer matches current schedulability. We study one exogenous binary schedulability unit under a bound on the joint probability of admission and unavailability. For a symmetric Markov state, we derive the stationary admission frontier for a fixed observation delay and apply finite likelihood allocation to a delay-tagged delivered record. A one-sided exact binomial endpoint calibrates each fitted policy, and exact enumeration confirms the per-policy confidence target in every tested parameter cell. A separate deterministic guard charges every unresolved admission against the realized allowance and bounds unavailable-state admissions at every prefix under truthful outcome feedback.
